Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note from whom and where you received them. If you would like to receive draft critique without going through the greenlighting process, please use the IRC chatrooms to request reviews.

item.title: Edit for SCP-5232: Edit for SCP-5232
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

nt:image-block
| name=SCP-5232
| caption=Image of SCP taken by CLASS-D before they had their eyes set on fire
]]

Item #: SCP-5232

Object Class: Safe

Threat Level: Blue

Special Containment Procedures: [All information regarding SCP-5170 is to be hidden from level 1 personnel or less if a person of such level accesses information regarding SCP-5170 they are to immediately receive Class-B Amnestics. SCP-5232 is to be kept in a 30m2 cell and protocol 202-5232-A

Protocol 202-5232-A forbids any foundation personnel to enter the cell unless they have already come within 30m of this SCP before the protocol was in place, tests with D-CLASS on SCP-5232 is still allowed as long as as the test is done by a level 3 or higher researcher.

Any cleaning of SCP-5232's cell is to be done by a D-CLASS janitor or any janitor who has come in contact with SCP-5232 beforehand and survived.

It has also been concluded impossible to destroy SCP-5232 and impossible to stop it rolling.

Description: [SCP-5232 is a six-sided silver dice of unknown origin. SCP-5232 does not show any anomalies properties until an entity (human, animal, plant and SCP all included) comes within 30m2 of the SCP, if an entity comes within 30m2 the dice will then proceed to roll itself, which tests have shown is completely randomized.

Once it has done this, if the higher value the number value displayed on the top of the dice, the higher level of damage the entity suffers. Tests show there is no way to cancel the anomalous effects and tests show the type of damage/death the entity suffers is also randomized. Also, a roll of one so far appears to guarantee no damage and a roll of six so far appears to guarantee instant death.]

« | SCP-5170 | »

CLASS-D: [D-4546B]

Researcher: [Nadiva Raghe]

Foreword: [Tesing if using a metallic clamp to stop the dice rolling will prove successful]

<Begin Log, [11:53]>

Researcher: [D-4546B please enter the cell and proceed to clamp the dice with the equipment you were given]

CLASS-D: [O K…what should I observe for?]

Researcher: [Anything out of the ordinary, NO more questions!]

Researcher: [Interesting. The dice appears to be melting the clamps and continue to roll itself]

CLASS-D: [I…Is that bad? It looks like its stopped.]

Researcher: [D-4546B I cannot see the number on the top of the dice, what does it show?]

CLASS-D: [It shows a six, why?]

Researcher: [Hmmm, ok I have an idea. D-4546B please proceed to leave the room. You have finished the test]

CLASS-D: [Oh…thank you Dr I hope I did we-]

CLASS-D: [AHHHHHHHHHhhh…]

Researcher: [Ok so it appears by leaves the area death still happens. D-4546B: Cause of Death: A currently unknown type of acid]

Researcher 2: [So Dr Nadiva how did the test go and what did we find out?]

Researcher: [Nothing especially interesting, the dice melted the clamp and then proceeded to still roll.]

Researcher 2: [Ok I shall bring in another D-CLASS, this time I want to see if the subject can be hidden from view and the dice will still roll.]

Researcher 2: [Very well, starting a new log]

<End Log, [12:07]>

Closing Statement: [The dice appeared to melt the clamp meaning test failed and leaving the area to stop the anomalous effects was unsuccessful]

CLASS-D: [D-4546E]

Researcher: [Dr Nadiva Raghe]

Foreword: [Testing if a physical barrier that blocks line of sight between entity and subject will stop the anomalous effects]

<Begin Log, [12:15]>

Interviewer: [D-4546E please proceed into the cell and make sure to keep that riot shield in front of you at all times.]

CLASS-D: [Yes Dr, now what exactly does this SCP do?]

Researcher: [Thats not for you to know, now enter the cell as instructed.]

CLASS-D: [So am I supposed to be looking for something happening? Or some changes in the room?]

Researcher: [D-4546E please position your body camera so I can observe the SCP.]

CLASS-D: [As you wish.]

CLASS-D: [It appears to be rolling itself, is this normal behaviour?]

Researcher: [Yes, now no more questions!]

CLASS-D: [Okay…]

Researcher: [D-4546E please can you tell me what number appears on the top of the dice?]

CLASS-D: [A five, is that nor-]

CLASS-D [Sorry, no more questions]

Researcher: [Nothing appears to be happening around you?]

CLASS-D: [No, but I am starting to feel a little strange.]

Researcher: [I'll get security to escort you to a medical room where we can issue a full-body scan]

CLASS-D: [AHHHh! Whats happened to me?!? I think my bones have melted!]

Researcher: [Please D-4546E remain calm. I'm calling a medical team to come and collect you for now please remain calm.]

CLASS-D [HOW CAN I REMAIN CALM WHEN MY BONES ARE LIQUID!?! AHHHH!]

Research: [Security I need D-4546E tranquillized immediately, thank you.]

Security: [Yes Dr Nadiva.]

Researcher: [Thank you, now please bring D-4546E to a medical bay to receive a full-body scan. D-4546E: Casualties: Liquidized bones]

<End Log, [12:21]>

Closing Statement: [Test unsuccessful however we now think that the higher the roll of the dice the more dangerous effects take place on the subject. However, more tests are required to prove that theory. It must also be noted that the security guard who tranquillized D-4546E had previously come in contact with SCP-5232 and had survived with only a broken leg as a casualty]

CLASS-D group: [D-4546F, D-4546G, D-4546H, D-4546I and D-4546K]

Researcher: [Dr Nadiva Raghe]

Foreword: [Testing if having multiple subjects in the cell affects how the anomaly works]

<Begin Log, [12:32]>

Researcher: [CLASS-Ds please enter the cell together at roughly the same time]

CLASS-D group: [Ok Dr Nadiva]

Researcher: [Thank you now D-4546H, please can you position your body camera so I can observe the SCP.]

D-4546H: [Yes Dr.]

Researcher: [Which one of you entered the cell first?]

D-4546I: [That would be me Dr, why do you ask?]

Researcher: [Please do not ask questions D-4546I, is that clear?]

D-4546I: [Yes, sorry Dr.]

D-4546F: [Dr the dice have stopped moving.]

Researcher: [Yes I can see that thank you. Its value is two, D-4546I do you feel anything strange or are you experiencing any pain?]

D-4546I: [Nothing that I've noticed so far. Oh wait, I appear to somehow have a scratch mark on my left shoulder. However, it's hardly bleeding]

Researcher: [Ok thank you D-4546I. D-4546H: Casualties: Scratch mark of unidentified species on the left shoulder, no serious damage.]

D-4546H: [Dr the dice is rolling again. Im positioning the camera now so you can observe it.]

Researcher: [I can not see the value still, please can you tell me what it shows]

D-4546I: [It shows a four Dr.]

Researcher: [Now D-4546H you were second to enter the cell?]

D-4546H: [Yes correct Dr.]

Researcher: [Please hand the camera over to D-4546G.]

D-4546H: [O…Ok, why what's going to happen to me?]

Researcher: [Please remain clam D-4546H I do not know what will happen, that is why you are here.]

CLASS-D: [Ok? Am I at least make it out alive.]

Researcher: [Most likely, yes. No more questions.]

D-4546H: [Im starting to feel hot, like burning hot. Oww I think I'm starting to burn!]

Researcher: [Please stay calm D-4546H and if you can not then please do not scream.]

D-4546H: [I can tr-]

Researcher: [It appears from the camera that D-4546H has passed out from the pain, is that correct? D-4546H: Casualties: Set on fire for 35 seconds and suffered 3rd-degree burns around the skull.]

D-4546G: [Seems that way Dr.]

Researcher: [Security please can you come in and escort D-4546H to a medical team and D-4546I to receive Class-B Amnestics, thank you]

Security: [Yes Dr Nadiva.]

Researcher: [The two of you that entered last please leave the cell and wait outside the door.]

D-4546G: [That would be me and D-4546F Dr. Should I leave the camera with D-4546K?]

Researcher: [Yes.]

D-4546K: [Okay, so I just wait to see what my fate is yes? And may I ask why they left the room?]

Researcher: [Did you not hear what I said to D-4546I?]

D-4546K: [Right yes, sorry.]

D-4546K: [Its rolled a 2, same as D-4546I]

Researcher: [Interesting, D-4546K please check your left shoulder for a scratch mark.]

D-4546K: [No scratch mark Dr, however, I think my ankle is sprained]

Researcher: [Ok so it seems even though the dice can roll the same value the effect is different. D-4546K: Casualties: Sprained ankle.]

D-4546K: [Dr the dice is rolling again although I am the only one in the room.]

Researcher: [Please can you get D-4546G and D-4546F back in the cell.]

D-4546K: [Yes. You too, Dr Nadiva wants you both back in here!]

Researcher: [The dice has stopped on a one, which one of you entered after D-4546K?]

D-4546G: [That would be me Dr I don't feel any pain or unease.]

Researcher: [Nothing at all?]

D-4546G: [Nothing Dr.]

Researcher: [Ok thank you D-4546K and D-4546G please leave the cell and Security will escort you to receive Amnestics.]

D-4546G: [Ok Dr thank you.]

D-4546F: [That leaves me now Dr? The dice has started rolling again. It's stopped on a six.]

Researcher: [Security please tranquillize D-4546F.]

D-4546F: [WHAT, why?!? What's going to hap-]

Security: [Done.]

Researcher: [D-4546F: Cause of Death: Several lead bullet shots to the cerebral cortex from. It is unknown where these bullets came from as there are no bullet holes in the wall of the cell.

<End Log, [13:01]>

Closing Statement: [Having several subjects in the cell did not affect how the anomalous effects functioned. We now know that the dice will roll one by one starting with who entered first]


No full drafts on the forums.

item.title: Tale critique: Stop Right There: Re: Tale critique: Stop Right There
item.content:encoded:
Hey, thanks for the crit. Don’t worry about the time. I hadn’t have the time myself.

+ Response
- Close

At first glance, I wasn’t sure what I was reading.

Well, it was a response to the terminal’s prompt to input the user’s ID code.

Unless this serves a purpose later in the article, I would rephrase/cut this.

Well, it was supposed to be someone for Freyberg to talk to. I figured that it would be a “morale-boosting” AI that at least doesn’t act robotic.

Ah. You see how it wasn’t clear the store was a lost-and-found office from the start?

Well, the store is a Foundation site masquerading as a normal bookstore. At the worst-case scenario, it wouldn’t have a lost-and-found “office”, but would store lost items.

Why did this happen?

I initially had attempted to explain it by writing that “the PoI allegedly threatened the officers” but it wouldn’t be realistic, as per your reasoning. I could replace it with the guards doing an impromptu interrogation, when they aren’t trained to do so.

what’s anomalous about both PoIs or the GoI they belong to

Well, they aren’t. They’re just normal conspiracy theorists who accidentally came up on the thing they were looking for.

So the Foundation raided and took over the base?

No. Sally’s was a Foundation site the whole time.

I think you need to highlight the stakes / danger of the scp or GoI MUCH earlier.

Thanks for pointing this out. The story was supposed to show the Foundation seeing large stakes that end up being false.

This shouldn’t be sufficient grounds for investigation.

Well, for the GoI. The site was always a Foundation facility. It’s just that a couple of people from a GoI had accidentally investigated an actual “anomaly facility”, and the Foundation is cranking up their defences over it.

A lot of the initial beats and tension you were aiming for did not come through during this Tale

I had written those into the tale initially, but cut them out since I couldn’t find a balance without overwhelming those reading, especially myself. The possibility of a mole was just a tool used to influence more power to the investigators.

I will attempt to revamp the tale into a proper tale format to see the changes I can do. Thanks again.

item.title: Explained SCP in need of review: Re: Explained SCP in need of review
item.content:encoded:
[+] Overall
[-] Overall

I think my biggest issue with this is it just feels very shallow: it doesn't really say much of anything or really do much of anything with the story, and so it ends up feeling almost more like an outline of the story than the full story itself?

Like, the idea of Agent Thompson investigating this cult, being forced to join it, and then marking this as explained to clear some of their heat and run away to join them isn't necessarily bad; but this feels kinda like it needs to actually play with Thompson trying to reduce heat here. Like, imagine if the second video log was followed up with a completely tone shifted set of logs; where like, the interview and the first video log are leading to the conclusion that something weird happens, followed by a log where something weird is implied to happen, followed by a couple of logs that are completely innocuous and show that there's nothing weird happening, before the ending came in?

It's possible this isn't the right fix: at the moment, it just, feels like it's missing the little spark of life it needs to work, y'know? It's all like competently put together, it just, doesn't grip a reader: it might be that Thompson doesn't have much character and so isn't really relatable, so his transition here feels empty because there's no sense of loss or anything? But also it just feels…very anticlimactic?

I wonder if part of this is that there's no stakes to it: the Lavinias aren't really like…planning much of anything, as far as can be seen, beyond a vague nod to them having like, embezzled two million and may be money laundering it, so Thompson getting suckered into joining them doesn't feel impactful because there's no sense of consequences to it: there's no big 'oh fuck they can [horrible thing they were planning] now' moment or anything, so it's just…a quiet ending that feels like it should be loud?

Iunno if it's just me, but the contents of Addendum C in combination with the ending make it feel too much like there's definitely anomalous stuff happening: this feels like it really needs to leave a reader feeling uncomfortable as they're not sure whether there's something bad happening under the surface or not, y'know? In part, the intro being so definitively "everything is okay here" feels like it doesn't quite lead us into the uncertainty right.

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

SCP-XXXX has been redesignated as Explained on 2019/7/19.

'has been' feels like the wrong tense: 'was' would read better here.

The individuals known as "Lavinia Hendrix" (formerly SCP-XXXX-1 through -14) have been administered amnestics and released. Observation is planned to continue until 2020/12/31.

I'm a little torn here: part of me feels like the date of the release of all the Lavinia Hendrix's would help here so we have more of an idea of the timeline but then you'd have three sentences containing a date at the end would feel awkward. Maybe just making it more clear that they were all released on the same date as the redesignation?

another two female humanoids

the repeated reference to 'humanoids' here makes it feel odd that this is explained: it implies 'human shaped but not human' to me generally since you'd just say 'humans' say if they were human, y'know?

How come… there are no men in this village?

there's two men in the background of the image of the scp that's implied to be pre-containment

"After embezzling State Bank ourout of 2 million".

i believe this is what you mean anyway

Nothing of particular interest was found at the librarian's house. Nothing even indirectly mentioning her grandmother. I will continue keeping an eye on the rest of the villagers for a while and if I don't find anything of value I will call for an Explained designation to be given to the anomaly.

This feels like a weird closing statement to the video recording; I think because contextually we haven't established that this video recording was taking place at the librarian's house

Nothing of value.

I'd either not include a closing statement or just use "N/A" here

[-] Line By Line

item.title: Looking for a review for Thermites: Re: Looking for a review for Thermites
item.content:encoded:
[+] Overall
[-] Overall

I'm going to be honest: this draft, in this state, is not a very interesting read. I would almost certainly downvote this if you posted it to the main site.

The core problem, for me, is that this is fundamentally a story of the conflict between D-32910 and Dr. Clyde, which is a fine idea, but it's barely explored. Like, the conflict fundamentally begins 2000 odd words in, with the extremely brief incident log; which is far too far in for the core plot to kick off. Well, there's technically a brief mention of it about 1.5k words in, at the end of the third sentence, but it's in an offhand comment Dr. Moore makes where we don't really have context for why he's mad at Clyde.

The conflict is then introduced, escalates and is resolved in ~1400 words and it's like…too shallow? Part of the problem is that we never really get a feel for what any of the characters are like as people, and so we don't really relate to them; and so their arguments aren't really that interesting. The rest of the problem is that the actual conflict is completely unrelatedable: we're given a few extremely brief snippets into it before the final confrontation and like,,,that confrontation is fine I guess but it doesn't feel climactic enough because the build up just isn't there.

It also feels really lacking in resolution: this feels like it should be a messy character drama with a more impactful ending than a quiet note saying 'Dr. Clyde was fired' followed by a weird note saying 'Dr. Moore was promoted'. In particular, the Moore promotion doesn't land cos he's almost completely a side character.

The complexity of the SCP feels….awkward here; like…it kinda explains why there's so much testing but none of the testing seems to really go anywhere or produce any kind of results. Like, 90% of the experiments here are 'we gave them metal, they melted it, we nodded and said very good' and there's a few times they send drones in but it really just…shows that the termites behave like termites? So like the actual tests just aren't very interesting, and it wouldn't necessarily be an issue but it serves to highlight that the character interactions aren't interesting either.

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

Sixteen SCP-XXXX-A instances (Designated as SCP-XXXX-A1 to A16) are kept at Site-XX high threat entomology wing.

'Designated' shouldn't be capitalised here; give Site-XX a number and 'kept in the' would be neater phrasing.

You also never actually define what -A is; the implication from later is that they're individual colonies but?

Each SCP-XXXX-A instance is kept in a 15m X 15m X 15m tungsten lined chamber.

this is a really big room; does it need to be this size? does it need to be tungsten?

Heat shielded monitoring equipment areis set up to alert onsite personnel of temperature increase ofby 50 C or higher.

Generally for groups defined using a singular noun (e.g. 'equipment', you use 'is' instead of 'are'.

Also celsius uses degrees: "50°C" is the correct notation here.

The following raw materials are to be provided monthly via an automated delivery system:

I'm…not really a fan of this list? There's one interesting item (scrap metal) but the rest feels like very generic stuff you'd give insects to keep 'em alive

Following incident.XXXX.15, no form of radioactive material is permitted for testing.

Generally if you're referring to a specific incident, you'd capitalise Incident

New testing materials may be requisitioned upon approval ofby the Site-XX director.

Since you haven't established any standard testing material, this feels…vague. Like in universe, a reader doesn't know if a material is a new testing material or not from this, and out-of-universe, it doesn't hint at anything beyond 'there is testing occurring' which we've already seen from the list and the previous sentence.

Only the approved personnel are to given access to internal containment chambers.

What are the 'internal containment chambers'? Are you trying to imply 'access to the interior of the containment chambers' actually, instead of 'there are outer and inner containment chambers'?

In the event of a containment breach the containment cell is to be flooded with a respiratory insecticide.

The paragraph this is attached to is largely about personnel: I'd probably move this somewhere else, perhaps to the end of the first paragraph which deals with the physical containment.

embedded media personnel

'personnel embedded in media organisations' would be a better way to phrase this to not imply 'personnel who are embedded media'

Neutralization is authorized should this prove impractical.

this feels vague about why movement would be impractical; I'm also questioning whether this much detail about moving stuff is necessary for the reader

SCP-XXXX differs in their large size and distinct coloration.

differs from what? each other? general Isoptera?

Adult workers average 40cm to 65cm. Soldiers range from 80cm to 90cm without body modifications. Their base color is a dark brown with red highlights.

This is excessively note-y imo; I'd probably try and mention the colour shortly after the colouration mention, and then talk about the adult workers and soldiers.

Also, average 40cm to 65cm in what? length? height? width?

SCP-XXXX-1 takes the form of a viscus fluid at room temperature.

I believe you mean 'viscous' (as in thick) here

SCP-XXXX can heat and maintain its internal temperature at around 2000c. How SCP-XXXX generates or maintains this temperature is unknown.

This is weirdly shoved into a paragraph that opens on the corrosive chemical produced by the SCP. I'd keep like ideas together.

Also see earlier comment about celsius. I'd probably not mention it being unknown and just leave it assumed.

If threatened, SCP-XXXX can expel SCP-XXXX-1 from its mouth or anus at high speed and distance.

What is 'high speed and distance' here? A meter? 300 meters? A light year?

Causing severe burns and impact trauma.

Sentence fragment: I'd probably leave this implied by it being corrosive and at high speed but *shrugs* your call; it at least needs to be e.g. "This can cause severe burns…" or tied into the previous sentence.

SCP-XXXX consumes a large verity of substance.

I believe you mean 'variety' here? Also 'substances'.

SCP-XXXX has shown a# preference to consume plant matter Plant mater, wood, animal dung, gasoline, crude oil, and [REDACTED].

This is a sucky redaction. There's not really anything hinting at what it is yet so it doesn't make us curious or think in a direct line of anything specific, and so it's just kinda there.

Also why would the in-universe Foundation redact this? Surely it'd be important for anyone cleared to read this file to know what kinds of things might cause the SCP to come charging at them to eat.

SCP-XXXX extracts carbon from its food and injects it into metals it consumes. This process results in high quality steel even regardless of the metals initial quality.

This phrasing implies that if it was fed say, pure aluminium, it would inject carbon into it to create a high carbon steel. You likely want to replace 'metal' with something more specific like 'iron'; though this would be a very basic understanding of metallurgy: 'high quality' is a vague term and often steels are alloyed with e.g. manganese or chromium for specific properties (e.g. improved strength or corrosion resistance) depending on need; and so 'high quality' doesn't necessarily mean 'more carbon'. Indeed, there's a point where you add too much carbon to steel and it gets all shitty again.

It was observed that SCP-XXXX instances became less aggressive to repeated visitors.

This is a wild thing to open an addendum with. It feels like this needs some context as to why there are repeat visitors in the first place and how it was detected.

Following this, a D-Class personal (D-32910) was handpicked for an long term experiment. D-32910 was assigned to a colony (SCP-XXXX-A7) for in depth testing of SCP-XXXX.

These sentences convey almost exactly the same idea and really it should be trimmed to one sentence that conveys both things.

D-32910 was chosen due to their educational background and compliant behavior. SCP-XXXX-A7 was the chosen for testing as it was the first "Foundation bred" colony. This was to reduce possible cross contamination from previous testing.

Not really sure either of these things are necessary; particularly with the D-32910 dossier immediately after this. Though, I guess the conterpoint is cut the dossier instead because it doesn't really convey anything new beyond this one sentence.

Dossier: D-32910

If the personal information of the D-Class is important enough to be attached to the file, it is too important to redact any of it. My inclination though is to cut this completely.

Experiment.XXXX.A7.1

Not really a fan of the tables here. They're very crushed: both between the tables since there's no empty lines and inside the tables since there's big blocks of text with no line breaks. A vertical quoteblock with the left column's headers would be more effective.

I'd also establish a standard test protocol before jumping into these so you don't have to cover the same 'd-class go in, puts test material down, observes for 30mins and leaves' info in all of these.

10/16/20██

Why is the year redacted here? How does knowing if it took place in 2001 or 2009 cause a security breach?

D-32910 will stay in the containment chamber for 30 minutes to make observations. If SCP-XXXX instances become aggressive

If the instances are aggressive, why is the D class being told to stay in the containment chamber at all? This feels like an unnecessary risk, particularly since they're trying to get the SCP to be more accustomed to the D-Class which they obviously can't do if they die.

D-32910 is to document their notes in the provided terminal.

Why don't they just record the test using cctv and then they don't need this to be done at all cos they can see what happened

D-32910 entered the containment chamber and approaches SCP-XXXX-A7.

We can assume that if the test protocol says this is to be the case, then they will do this.

At this point members of SCP-XXXX-A7 notices D-32910 and take an aggressive stance.

Aggressive stance should lead to D-32910 being signalled to stop; the information is backwards here.

SCP-XXXX instances melted and consumed it entirely.

this phrasing implies the SCP-XXXX instances melted, not that they melted the gold. Something like "SCP-XXXX instances melted the gold before consuming it entirely." would be clearer.

D-32910 remained in the containment chamber for the remainder of the time while keeping their distance as instructed. SCP-XXXX instances remained pacified for the remainder of the test.

I'd try to restructure this to avoid the repetition of 'remained'/'remainder'

To be honest, I would cut this bit; it can be assumed from the Protocol and it means you can focus on the interesting bits as opposed to 'the test went according to protocol'.

more like wasps or hornets than termites. Also, can I get some cooling in that suit?

no suit was mentioned. Missing capital at the start of the first sentence.

The instance seen above has been given the tentative title of "Director".

Why? There was no indication that that would fit their role.

Dr. Clyde connected to the device remotely and performed standard diagnostics.

This feels like it gets into unnecessary levels of detail to convey 'we setup a probe'. I'm also unclear on why they didn't pilot the probe into the nest: it feels like having the D-Class set it up in there is unnecessary.

Slight static is heard from the probes microphones.

Okay? I don't know why this is mentioned.

After 5 minutes the gold has been formed into a near a cube roughly 7mm in size.

This is…tiny? Like these things are 40cm long so it feels…odd for them to make the cube this small?

A Director instance similar to the one seen in Experiment.XXXX.A7.2. Approaches

unnecessary capitalisation of 'approaches'.

to trail the instance; However further progress

unnecessary capitalisation of 'however'

The probe packed by D-32910. D-32910 exits the containment chamber with the RLSOP.

I'd cut this, we can assume the probe is removed successfully.

Director instances seem disregard this and take materials by force.” -Dr. Clyde

Every other time, you bolded the name of the people here. I would probably leave them unbolded tbh.

While much older workers perform more complex tasks.

Sentence fragment that should be part of the previous sentence.

Workers will provide food and gifts to older members in exchange for goods or services.

We don't need a list of examples here.

You have 0 unread emails

I'd put the email into a quote block to clearly segment it as a thing. The How to Write an SCP guide shows how to do it using divs in the 'Interview Template' in the 'Templates' tab; which is far easier than using >

Upon approval from the site director, we have been given approval for D-32910 to assist in lab testing.

Repetition of them getting approval is unnecessary

In addition D-32910 has been approved for an additional 2 hours a day forof personal testing on individual SCP-XXXX instances if desired, given that the following requirements are met:

'Additional' implies the D-class was getting personal testing time already; the D-Class should not under any circumstances be getting personal testing time.

Any Insubordination, aggression, misbehavior

Insubordination should not be capitalised here

Site-19 Site-XX high threat entomology wing

repeated site name

Over a four-month period D-32910, performed over ███ personal tests.

comma should be after period, not where it is. This is a wack redaction too.

Incident.XXXX.27 VIDEO LOG

This incident conveys so little to the reader that it's not worth keeping it in this state. It really needs to highlight why the altercation happened so that the Post Incident interview following it can build off that rather than just 'there is some kind of incident' followed by 'please exposit everything that happened'

Post incident interview - D-32910

I'd add an empty line between each line of dialogue. Using "> " (note the space after the >) on a line will allow an empty line to be added.

<Begin Log, 3/5/20██ 13:54>

yet another bad redaction.

question, should end in a question mark

The door is heard opening and closing as Dr. Webers assistant enters the room and places a bottle of water on the table, followed by the door opening and closing once more as they leave.

I'd put actions like this in italics to distinguish them more from text.

I told him he was being a [expletive removed].

you are allowed to swear in a scp article.

He began shouting at me, and then he brought up ████.

Since this is redacted, a reader's immediate reaction is 'wait what'. If this person had been given a name, we would be a lot more likely to realise what you mean here.

Report.XXXX.21

The use of styling here is actively distracting considering there's not really any reason for it.

I will not and cannot allow personal altercations to impact the work done within Foundation.

The use of 'I will' makes this feel a lot less weighty in the judgement than a more passive construction like:

Personal alteractions cannot be allowed to impact the work done within the Foundation.

would convey.

Dr. Clyde has been reprimanded for unprofessional behavior and unauthorized disclosure of classified information.

I'm not sure what 'unauthorized disclosure of classified information' is referring to like, the D-Class almost certainly already knows about them killing redacted so??

Dr. Moore was absent due to being bitten by an SCP-████ instance thus requiring medical leave.

Unnecessary.

chamber of the nest. With the object.

The end sentence should be part of the previous sentence.

Today is Dr. Moores last day on the SCP-XXXX project

This feels like a weird place for the ending to go.
